france24fr.description:
Les Calédoniens ont voté dans le calme dimanche 28 juin pour les premières élections provinciales depuis 2019, un scrutin appelé à redessiner les rapports de force politiques de l'archipel et à peser sur les négociations sur son avenir institutionnel, dans l'impasse depuis les émeutes meurtrières de mai 2024.

france24fr.title: Afrique du Sud - Canada : suivez en direct le premier 16e de finale du Mondial
france24fr.description: Les 16es de finale débutent dimanche à Los Angeles avec le match opposant le Canada, co-organisateur de cette Coupe du monde, à l'Afrique du Sud. Pour continuer à tracer leur route dans cette compétition, les Canucks vont profiter du retour bienvenu de leur capitaine Alphonso Davies, blessé jusque-là. Les deux équipes ont terminé deuxièmes de leurs groupes respectifs, mais le Canada a sans doute laissé une meilleure impression. Suivez cette rencontre en direct sur le site de France 24.

france24fr.title: Avec 9 pays qualifiés en 16es, le football africain vit "un Mondial historique"
france24fr.description: Un seul pays africain manque à l’appel à l’heure où débutent les 16es de finale de la Coupe du monde : la Tunisie. Tous les autres ont réussi à se qualifier pour la suite de la compétition. Premier pays africain à entrer en lice dans cette phase finale, l'Afrique du Sud qui affrontera le Canada, dimanche soir.

france24fr.title: Séismes au Venezuela, démission de Starmer, statue de Lumumba au Mondial : la semaine en images

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la RD Congo qualifiée, les supporters rêvent des demi-finales
france24fr.description: Les supporters de la RD Congo célèbrent la qualification des Léopards à Atlanta et affichent leurs ambitions avant le quart de finale contre l'Angleterre. Plusieurs regrettent également l'absence du célèbre supporter Lumumba Vea, privé de visa pour entrer aux États-Unis.

france24fr.title: Cuba se tourne vers l'énergie solaire face au blocus énergétique des États-Unis
france24fr.description: Depuis que Washington impose un blocus pétrolier de facto à la Havane, l'île vit au rythme des coupures de courant. Les habitants se tournent vers de nouvelles solutions, dont l'énergie solaire.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la Coupe du monde suivie à Gaza
france24fr.description: À Gaza, les matchs de la Coupe du monde sont diffusés dans des cafés improvisés. Une parenthèse dans un quotidien éprouvant.

france24fr.title: Venezuela : des sauveteurs du monde entier arrivent au Venezuela
france24fr.description: Le temps presse pour retrouver des survivants plus de 72 heures après le double séisme au Venezuela dont le bilan continue de s'alourdir. Des secouristes du monde entier viennent en aide à la population, rapporte notre correspondante Alice Campaignolle.

france24fr.title: États-Unis et Iran poursuivent leurs bombardements et s'accusent mutuellement
france24fr.description: Les États-Unis et l'Iran poursuivent leurs bombardements dans le ⁠Golfe, chacun accusant ​l'autre de violer un protocole d'accord de plus en plus précaire, signé il y a moins de deux semaines et censé mettre fin à près de ​quatre mois de conflit entre les deux pays.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : arbitrage, pauses fraîcheur, pelouse... les tops et les flops de la phase de groupes
france24fr.description: La phase de groupes du Mondial 2026 a pris fin dimanche après presque trois semaines de compétition. À mi-parcours, cette Coupe du monde nouveau format donne à voir du bon et du moins bon : les arbitres qui laissent beaucoup plus jouer, les pauses fraîcheurs... France 24 fait ses tops et ses flops à l'issue des 72 premiers matches de la compétition.

france24fr.title: Nouvelle-Calédonie : les électeurs aux urnes pour un scrutin décisif
france24fr.description: Les Calédoniens ont commencé à voter dimanche 28 juin pour les premières élections provinciales depuis 2019, un scrutin qui doit redessiner les rapports de force politiques de l'archipel et peser sur les négociations à venir sur son avenir institutionnel, dans l'impasse depuis les émeutes de 2024. france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : début des 16es de finale ce soir
france24fr.description: Une nouvelle phase débute dans cette Coupe du monde de football : celle des 16es de finale. Ce soir, première rencontre entre l'Afrique du Sud et le Canada. Nous revenons sur les moments forts de cette phase de poules avec notre envoyé spécial Cédric Ferreira.

france24fr.title: Coupe du monde 2026 : la Colombie termine devant des Portugais décevants
france24fr.description: Le Portugal devait battre la Colombie pour récupérer la première place du groupe K. Mais c’est la Colombie qui était la plus proche de l’emporter. Les deux équipes se sont finalement quittées sur un score nul.

spiegel.description: Seit mehr als zehn Jahren verbieten türkische Behörden die Pride-Parade in Istanbul. Dieses Mal haben sie sogar die Innenstadt abgesperrt. Dennoch kam es zu Demonstrationen, die aber schnell unterbunden wurden.

spiegel.title: Rätsel des Alltags: Warum haben manche Münzen Rillen am Rand?
spiegel.description: 50-Cent-Stücke sind wellenförmig geprägt, 1-Euro-Münzen haben unterbrochene Rillen. Auf 2-Euro-Stücken ist sogar ein Schriftzug am Rand zu lesen. Wozu ist das gut? DEIN SPIEGEL erklärt’s.

spiegel.title: Polen: 10.000 Zloty pro Jahr für jedes NS-Opfer gefordert
spiegel.description: Polen drängt laut einem Medienbericht weiter auf eine Entschädigung von NS-Opfern durch Deutschland. Die Forderung der aktuellen Regierung ist deutlich moderater als die der Vorgänger – die Finanzierung dennoch offen.

spiegel.title: Fußball WM: Florian Wirtz und Jamal Musiala – wann kommt ihre große Stunde?
spiegel.description: Es war bisher nicht das Turnier der beiden deutschen Supertalente Jamal Musiala und Florian Wirtz. Trotzdem genießen sie Rückhalt von den Verantwortlichen. Noch.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 News heute: Südkoreas Präsident ledert nach WM-Aus gegen Verband und Nationaltrainer
spiegel.description: Der Frust in Südkorea ist nach dem verpassten Einzug in die K.-o.-Runde groß. Der Präsident fordert eine Untersuchung des Scheiterns und erhebt schwere Vorwürfe. Und: Uruguays Spieler mussten ihre Heimreise selbst organisieren. Alles Wichtige zur WM.

spiegel.title: Frankreich: Elf Tote bei Flugzeugabsturz bei Nancy
spiegel.description: Im Osten Frankreichs ist ein ziviles Flugzeug abgestürzt, mehrere Menschen starben. Offenbar handelt es sich zum Teil um Krankenpfleger, die einen Fallschirmsprung gebucht hatten.

spiegel.title: Google-KI-Chef Koray Kavukcuoglu: Wie fühlt es sich an, den teuersten Job bei Google zu haben?
spiegel.description: Er leitet bei Google maßgeblich die Entwicklung von künstlicher Intelligenz. Sein Ziel ist eine KI, die so gut ist wie der Mensch. Seine Abteilung gibt Hunderte Milliarden Dollar aus. Hier erzählt er, was er damit vorhat.

spiegel.title: Ermittler untersuchen Absturz von Hubschrauber in Saudi-Arabien mit 14 Toten
spiegel.description: Bei dem Absturz eines Hubschraubers des Ölkonzerns Aramco an ​der saudi-arabischen Golfküste sind 14 Menschen gestorben. Die Ermittlungen laufen.

spiegel.title: WM 2026: Welcher Sender überträgt welches Sechzehntelfinale?
spiegel.description: Das Turnier in den USA, Mexiko und Kanada startet in die heiße Phase: Wer gewinnt, ist weiter – wer verliert, fährt heim. Wo Sie die Runde der letzten 32 Teams verfolgen können, erfahren Sie hier.

spiegel.title: Ärztechef fordert deutlich höhere Preise für Zigaretten und Spirituosen
spiegel.description: Genussgifte teurer und damit unerschwinglich für junge Leute machen: Auf diese Strategie setzt die Kassenärztliche Bundesvereinigung. 20 Euro für eine Schachtel Zigaretten soll die neue Schmerzgrenze sein.

spiegel.title: Schulkinder sehen, wie Biber vom Zug erfasst wird
spiegel.description: Der Anblick war schockierend: Nach einem Biber-Unfall im bayerischen Türkenfeld mussten mehrere Augenzeugen psychologisch betreut werden.

observador.title: Astronauta Luca Parmitano: "Sinto que já estou na Lua"
observador.description: Em entrevista ao Observador, o astronauta da ESA que vai ser o piloto na Artemis III destaca a importância da última missão do programa da NASA que vai terminar com o regresso da humanidade à Lua.

observador.title: Japonês Ai Ogura estreia-se a vencer em MotoGP
observador.description: Ogura bateu o companheiro de equipa na Trackhouse, o espanhol Raul Fernández (Aprilia), por 2,004 segundos, com o espanhol Jorge Martín (Aprilia) a ficar em terceiro, a 3,512.

observador.title: 16h. Carneiro acusa o Governo de prejudicar a economia
observador.description: O líder socialista faz declarações na abertura da reunião da Comissão Nacional do PS. Ainda, a onda de calor na Europa causou a morte de mil e 300 pessoas, só na última semana.

observador.title: Rock in Rio Lisboa regressa ao Parque Tejo em 2028
observador.description: Na "maior edição de sempre do festival", a organização estima que tenham passado cerca de 330 mil pessoas pelo recinto ao longo de quatro dias.

observador.title: Câmara de Braga quer acabar com trotinetes partilhadas
observador.description: Presidente da Câmara de Braga diz que proposta vai ser apresentada esta segunda-feira: "Não podemos ignorar os inúmeros casos de acidentes com trotinetas."

observador.title: Onda de calor na Europa matou 1.300 pessoas na última semana
observador.description: Diretor-geral da Organização Mundial de Saúde assinalou que o continente europeu é o que regista o mais rápido aquecimento, duas vezes mais do que a média global.

observador.title: Russell escreveu o guião mas Max não foi só ator secundário
observador.description: Ferrari não mostrou em corrida o que prometera na qualificação, Mercedes voltou a ser mais forte mas houve uma surpresa chamada Max Verstappen a impedir nova dobradinha dos ingleses em Spielberg.

observador.title: Ogier vence Rali da Acrópole, na Grécia
observador.description: Ogier terminou a prova grega com 58,3 segundos de vantagem sobre o belga Thierry Neuville (Hyundai) e o japonês Takamoto Katsuta (Hyundai i20) ficou em terceiro, a 3.04,8 minutos do vencedor.

observador.title: Quem é Schroyer, o polícia de trânsito que vai liderar o ICE
observador.description: Numa palavra, segundo Donald Trump, Lance Schroyer é um "PATRIOTA". Mas a nomeação mereceu a oposição do antigo czar da fronteira do Presidente. Lance chegou ao ICE em março, como conselheiro.

observador.title: 15h. 11 pessoas morreram numa queda de um avião em França
observador.description: O avião tinha descolado do aeródromo de Nancy Essey e caiu numa zona residencial. Ainda, o Papa Leão XIV agradece pela assistência ao povo venezuelano depois dos sismos de quarta-feira.

observador.title: Krasznahorkai, Orbán e o Nobel: “Ainda não acredito”
observador.description: O escritor húngaro está no Porto para o festival Babell. Ao Observador, fala do Nobel com incredulidade, da queda de Orbán com alívio e da esperança como um erro cósmico — não moral.

observador.title: PS/Madeira exige explicações sobre custos com novo hospital
observador.description: PS "vai continuar a insistir que este processo das obras do hospital tem de ser transparente" e que o executivo tem a obrigação legal de disponibilizar a documentação que justifique aumento do custo.

observador.title: 14h. Irão diz que mantém controlo sobre Estreito de Ormuz
observador.description: Teerão exige também que Washington pressione Israel a retirar-se do Líbano. Ainda, subiu para 51... o número de vítimas mortais entre portugueses e lusodescendentes na Venezuela.

observador.title: Vai ficar mais caro comprar na Shein e Temu. O que muda?
observador.description: A partir de 1 de julho, entram em cena novas regras para compras até 150 euros de artigos que venham de fora da União Europeia. A medida quer pôr mão no disparo de encomendas das plataformas chinesas.

observador.title: Zizou Bergs vence torneio de ténis de Eastbourne
observador.description: O atual 48.º classificado do ranking tinha perdido as duas finais anteriormente disputadas, ambas no ano passado, nomeadamente em 's-Hertogenbosch, também em relva.

observador.title: Alverca oficializa saída do treinador Custódio Castro
observador.description: Custódio Castro assumiu a equipa no início da época passada, guiando os alverquenses ao 11.º lugar da I Liga e à desejada manutenção no primeiro escalão um ano após a subida.

observador.title: 13h. Venezuela. Número de portugueses mortos sobe para 51
observador.description: São 44 lusodescendentes, 6 portugueses (nacionais) e 1 português por casamento. Ainda, o Papa Leão 14 agradece a todos os que têm ajudado a Venezuela depois dos sismos desta semana.

observador.title: Sismos. Oposição na Venezuela denuncia proibições de ajudar
observador.description: Oposição diz-se proibida de usar termo "centro de doação". Há vídeos que mostram polícia a desmobilizar recolhas. Especialistas alertam que ajuda humanitária alimenta luta política. E dos dois lados.

elpais.title: Venezuela afronta la catástrofe con el Estado sobrepasado
elpais.description: Tutelado por Estados Unidos, sin libre acceso a sus ingresos y con un sistema que ya operaba al límite, el país sudamericano afronta sus horas más difíciles

elpais.title: Última hora del terremoto en Venezuela, en directo | Exteriores eleva a 9 la cifra de españoles fallecidos y a 152 la de desaparecidos en el doble terremoto de Venezuela
elpais.description: Asciende a 1.430 el número de muertos por los seísmos y a 3.238 la de heridos | Delcy Rodríguez visita a los brigadistas internacionales y comunica que ayer rescataron a 33 personas

elpais.title: Videoanálisis |“Los vecinos sacan los cascotes con sus propias manos. Es una precariedad absoluta”
elpais.description: La corresponsal de EL PAÍS en la región andina describe una situación durísima tras el doble sismo del miércoles en Venezuela, con pocos medios y falta de coordinación en las tareas de rescate

elpais.title: Radiografía de la desconfianza ciudadana en la justicia: “El sistema disciplinario no funciona”
elpais.description: Magistrados y catedráticos analizan las decisiones  judiciales más controvertidas y los déficits de control sobre los jueces

elpais.title: Ro Khanna, el demócrata al que Elon Musk quiere en la cárcel: “El dinero tiene secuestrada la política en Estados Unidos”
elpais.description: El congresista, representante por Silicon Valley, lidera la cruzada contra Trump para liberar los papeles de Epstein y no descarta presentarse a la presidencia en 2028. “No van a callarme”, advierte

elpais.title: Colombia muestra las debilidades del plan de Roberto Martínez a la medida de Cristiano Ronaldo
elpais.description: La Seleção, que rascó un empate gracias a la exhibición de Diogo Costa tras ser sometida por su rival, queda segunda de grupo y cae en una zona del cuadro llena de minas con Croacia en dieciseisavos y un posible cruce contra España después

elpais.title: Austria es el rival de España en dieciseisavos tras un empate de locos contra Argelia
elpais.description: El agónico 3-3 logrado en Kansas clasifica a los dos equipos y deja fuera del Mundial a Irán

elpais.title: ¿Con quién jugará España? Consulte el cuadro final y todos los cruces de dieciseisavos
elpais.description: Un interactivo de EL PAÍS muestra el camino de cada selección hasta la final

elpais.title: La Argentina B también necesita a Leo Messi para rendir a Jordania
elpais.description: La estrella albiceleste sentencia con su sexto gol un partido que había arrancado bien el equipo de suplentes de Scaloni

elpais.title: El Museo Sorolla de Madrid está de mudanza: descubrimos su nueva cara
elpais.description: Hemos seguido, paso a paso, su ampliación y remodelación. Los nuevos espacios, ubicados en un antiguo taller de coches, abrirán sus puertas tras el verano, antes de que finalice la rehabilitación de la casa

elpais.title: Un catedrático español denuncia fraude masivo con IA en un examen en la Universidad de Brown: “La integridad académica está en peligro”
elpais.description: El reconocido economista Roberto Serrano tiene “evidencias abrumadoras” de que sus estudiantes han copiado. Cree que hay que abrir un debate profundo para que esta tecnología no acabe con la enseñanza superior

elpais.title: Madonna: el manual de resistencia lo inventó ella
elpais.description: La cantante, que edita disco el 3 de julio, pasó de coger comida de la basura a ser la mayor estrella del pop, cima que alcanzó con un arma: acorazar su libertad

elpais.title: El misterio de Agatha Christie: la autora más vendida, imitada e incomprendida de la literatura universal
elpais.description: En el centenario de la publicación de ‘El asesinato de Roger Ackroyd’, la novela que la catapultó a la fama, desentrañamos las claves de una autora única, prolífica y compleja que va mucho más allá de los 2.000 millones de libros vendidos

elpais.title: Adriana Ugarte: “Cuando pensé que podría ser feliz sin ser actriz, amé esta profesión como nunca”
elpais.description: Tras un parón para reconstruirse, la actriz acepta solo papeles que le llegan al corazón, como el de la circense Pinito del Oro en su próxima película ‘Tal vez’. Matriculada en Filosofía, vive en el campo, rescata gatos y forma parte de la comunidad Artistas con Palestina

elpais.title: Francia registra 1.000 fallecidos más en los últimos días atribuibles a la ola de calor
elpais.description: La mortalidad aumentó entre el martes y el jueves, en pleno pico de la canícula, según la agencia nacional de salud pública, y los decesos en domicilios han crecido un 40%, aunque son cifras aún provisionales

elpais.title: Cuando el Parlamento se vacía
elpais.description: Las razones de orden político existen y operan en las instituciones democráticas. Mirar a otro lado no las elimina; solo nos hace más vulnerables a ellas

elpais.title: Nacidos para triunfar
elpais.description: Los padres de hoy contagian a sus hijos el estrés que provoca la necesidad de ser los mejores

elpais.title: Lo humano
elpais.description: Todo esto, lo bueno y lo malo, desaparecerá como lágrimas en la lluvia, según la famosa frase del replicante de ‘Blade Runner’

nyt.title: Trump Cut a Billion-Dollar Mining Deal. His Sons Stand to Profit.

nyt.title: Kazakhstan’s Leader Deepens U.S. Ties, Saying Trump Was ‘Sent by Heaven’
nyt.description: The Central Asian nation is aggressively courting President Trump’s Washington to counterbalance its powerful neighbors, Russia and China.

nyt.title: What Life Is Like in Dahiya Amid a Hezbollah-Israel Truce in Lebanon
nyt.description: Dahiya, a sprawling area and Hezbollah stronghold, is stirring back to life amid a tense truce with Israel. “This war has brought so much loss,” one resident said.

nyt.title: Here’s What to Know About the Standoff in the Strait of Hormuz
nyt.description: The United States and Iran have engaged in rounds of attacks and counterattacks in recent days, eroding hopes for a quick return to normalcy in the Middle East.

nyt.title: White House Secretly Swayed Board Meant to Protect Federal Workers From Unfair Firings
nyt.description: Behind the scenes, the Trump White House went to extensive lengths to advance its theory of executive power, potentially giving the president remarkable leeway to install loyalists at nearly every echelon of government.

nyt.title: Rats, Leaks and Broken Elevators: Repair Backlog Plagues Federal Buildings
nyt.description: After decades, deferred maintenance totals an estimated $50 billion. But getting repair funds from Congress is a laborious process.

nyt.title: Trump Picks Lance Schroyer as New ICE Director
nyt.description: The president said he was nominating Lance Schroyer, an adviser to Markwayne Mullin, the D.H.S. secretary, to lead the high-profile agency.

nyt.title: 12 Hours With Venezuelan Doctors Searching for Earthquake Survivors
nyt.description: A medical team set out from the capital to rescue people in the hardest-hit part of the disaster zone, La Guaira. They found silence in the ruins instead.

nyt.title: A Rush of Volunteers in Venezuela Has Slowed Rescue Efforts
nyt.description: The outpouring of volunteer aid after Venezuela’s earthquakes clogged the only road into the disaster zone, delaying rescue crews.

nyt.title: Colorado’s Primary for Governor Pivots to Trump and Who Will Fight Him
nyt.description: The Democratic primary on Tuesday is likely to decide the next governor, and Senator Michael Bennet, once seen as a shoo-in, is in a dogfight with Attorney General Phil Weiser.

nyt.title: What’s the Hottest Spot in New York for Campaigning? The Club.
nyt.description: Zohran Mamdani did it last year. So did Claire Valdez in her recent run for Congress. Some candidates are campaigning after dark to court young voters.

nyt.title: Julia Letlow, Lifted by Trump, Wins Republican Senate Runoff in Louisiana
nyt.description: If she reaches the Senate, Ms. Letlow would replace Senator Bill Cassidy and become the first G.O.P. woman to represent Louisiana in the chamber.

nyt.title: ‘After About 10 Minutes, a Car Pulled Up to the Traffic Light’
nyt.description: Friends of Metropolitan Diary, including the writer Candace Bushnell and the actor Ken Leung of “Industry,” share their stories to mark the column’s 50th anniversary.

nyt.title: How Polymarket Traders Revolted Over One Silly Syllable
nyt.description: How one silly syllable ignited a bitter dispute over the nature of reality on Polymarket.

nyt.title: The Hamptons’ Essential Luxury Good: Human Labor

nyt.description: The firefighters died in a blaze in Colorado. Fires have swept the arid border region after a warm winter produced less snow than normal.

npr.title: Trade tensions shake up Brazil's caipirinha spirit
npr.description: U.S. tariff pressure is pushing Europe and Brazil closer—opening new global doors for everything from aircraft parts to Brazil's cachaça, the base of the caipirinha.

npr.title: 'If you are alive, make any noise': Venezuela searches rubble on day 4
npr.description: Rescue teams are racing against time after twin earthquakes killed more than 1,400 people and left tens of thousands unaccounted for.

npr.title: Venezuela races to find survivors
npr.description: The search for survivors is entering a critical stage in Venezuela. NPR'S Eyder Peralta reports from La Guaira where rescue crews are still hoping to find people alive.

npr.description: The ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran is being tested after new attacks in the Strait of Hormuz. Mideast expert Paul Salem explains what's happened and whether the deal can still hold.

npr.description: Covering an Ebola outbreak means taking extra precautions. In this Reporter's Notebook, NPR's Emmet Livingstone takes us behind the reporting in eastern Congo.

npr.title: Uzbekistan makes its World Cup debut, a first for Central Asia
npr.description: The country is the first Central Asian nation to qualify for the World Cup, and Uzbek fans have reveled in showcasing their country and culture. The country's president calls the team a symbol of the "new Uzbekistan."

npr.title: A historian analyzes whether Ukraine has a localized advantage in modern combat power
npr.description: NPR's Scott Simon talks with strategic studies professor Phillips O'Brien of St Andrew's University in Scotland about whether Ukraine has gained the upper hand in the fight against Russia.

npr.title: Inside a secretive Ukrainian team launching deep drone strikes at Russia
npr.description: Ukraine's long-range drones are striking deep inside Russia, up to 1,200 miles away, hitting oil refineries and depots. NPR recently spent time with one of the Ukrainian strike teams launching drones at Russian targets.

npr.title: Venezuelans in Colombia scramble to send aid as earthquakes death toll increases
npr.description: Aid efforts are intensifying after twin earthquakes killed over 1,400 in Venezuela, with international teams arriving but a slow government response hampering relief on the ground.

npr.title: There's a beef about beef at the World Cup, as Argentina fans pour into Texas
npr.description: It's about who produces the best, most succulent steaks, and how to prepare the meat. Argentina and Texas are two of the top cattle-raising areas of the world, where steak is deeply ingrained in diet and culture.

lanacion.title: Compararon la risa de los niños y de los simios: encontraron una coincidencia reveladora

phys-org.description: For decades, scientists have searched for a clear link between the sun's explosive storms and the weather that occurs on Earth. A breakthrough study from the University of New Hampshire reveals that in the hours and days following a solar storm, parts of North America can see sharp changes in the weather—such as declines in precipitation—and the more powerful the storm, the more dramatic the shift.

phys-org.title: Scientists uncover evolutionary edge behind plant invasions

The paper outlining this research was published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters on June 12.

phys-org.title: Oxygen atoms in 15‑million‑year‑old giant eggshells reveal how plants reacted to a hotter Earth

This enables them to flourish in a wide variety of habitats, including deserts, swamps, open grasslands, woodlands and tropical forests.

The researchers made their findings available to the Los Angeles Public Health Department over the course of the study.

phys-org.title: New research identifies types of dishonesty that occur in a relationship—and their consequences

New research from the University of Copenhagen shows that while dishonesty between partners often fuels distrust and resentment, it may also, in some cases, help couples solve issues and repair their bond.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers

One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway

But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime

Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence

proj-syn.title: Is a European Single Market for Energy Such a Good Idea?
proj-syn.description: Although textbook microeconomics shows why less energy-market fragmentation would be better for Europe as a whole, that does not mean it would be a good deal for countries producing low-carbon electricity at minimal marginal cost. In fact, if more integration creates free riders, the political backlash could be profound.

proj-syn.title: China’s Failed Rebalancing
proj-syn.description: When China’s leaders first acknowledged the need to rebalance the economy nearly two decades ago, it seemed like a matter of when, not if. But with the household consumption share of Chinese GDP remaining stubbornly low, officials’ promises to boost domestic demand have lost all credibility.

proj-syn.title: Crowning a Healthy Populism
proj-syn.description: Although recent political mobilizations in Hungary, Albania, and other parts of Central and Eastern Europe could be described as populist and nationalist, they have little in common with the aggressive ethnonationalism that MAGA professes. Could they be a model for a new form of politics?

proj-syn.title: Why Rules-Based Orders Fail
proj-syn.description: For a brief period after the Cold War, Americans persuaded themselves that the liberal order had become self-sustaining. And yet, any rules-based system elaborate enough to govern and interpret its own operations will eventually confront questions that its rules cannot answer.

proj-syn.title: The Tide Is Turning Against Russia
proj-syn.description: With Ukraine reclaiming territory, mounting drone strikes deep in Russian territory, and draining Russia’s coffers, Vladimir Putin would do well to seek a negotiated freeze to the conflict. But there is no guarantee that he will, not least because he might not grasp the situation Russia is in.

proj-syn.title: Managing Sino-American Interdependence
proj-syn.description: At their summit last month, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping seemed to recognize that they are in the same boat. If either the United States or China tries to cripple or decouple from the other, it will harm its own firms, consumers, financial markets, and innovation ecosystem.

proj-syn.title: Who Gains in an AI-Supercharged Economy?
proj-syn.description: If AI delivers as promised and fundamentally transforms the economy, we will have moved from the current investment phase, where AI builders dominate, to one where AI users will reap the greatest reward. That is what happens every time an innovation becomes a general-purpose technology.

proj-syn.title: Development in a Time of Disruption
proj-syn.description: Once firms and economies ascend to market dominance, they often kick away the ladder behind them and erect barriers to market entry to stymie would-be challengers. But developing countries can and do leapfrog incumbent technologies, and conditions for doing so may be particularly favorable now.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Un-American Capitalism
proj-syn.description: The current US administration's openly corrupt style of crony capitalism is the antithesis of the institutional foundation on which the US economy was built. The winners in the new oligarchic competition are not those who make the best products, but rather those who are best at flattering the mad king.

proj-syn.title: Can the Manchester Model Save Britain?
proj-syn.description: Following a decades-long effort to lay the foundations for economic dynamism, Greater Manchester has become the UK’s fastest-growing region. While the Manchester model cannot be precisely replicated at the national level, it does carry important lessons for outgoing Prime Minister Keir Starmer's likely successor.

proj-syn.title: How Trillionaires Are Really Made
proj-syn.description: Some may argue that the world’s first trillionaire is a story of technological triumph and a win for American capitalism. But markets have not bet on cutting-edge technology or a company too big to fail, but rather on the idea of a mega-monopolist with wealth and influence so vast that the US government will not allow him to fail.

proj-syn.title: Cities Show How Climate Action Makes Life Better
proj-syn.description: Cities have shown that a combination of adaptation measures and energy efficiency can save lives, improve well-being, reduce energy costs, and create conditions for sustainable growth. A new partnership seeks to help mayors and city leaders scale up these efforts through technical and financial assistance.

proj-syn.title: The Myth of Global Chaos
proj-syn.description: Today’s seemingly nonstop international tumult is not as unintelligible as it seems. What pundits lazily describe as chaos is the culmination of developments that were long in the making and arrived at a time when the international system was no longer able to prevent or mitigate geopolitical shocks.

proj-syn.title: The Microfinance Debate Is Missing the Point
proj-syn.description: For too long, policymakers, economists, and investors have focused on whether microfinance actually helps people, reducing a complex issue to a meaningless yes-or-no verdict. The most important questions concern how loans are designed, delivered, and regulated, who receives them, and what they are used for.

proj-syn.title: Turning Latin America’s Resilience Into Growth
proj-syn.description: Economic stabilization has been a significant achievement for Latin America and the Caribbean, a region with a long history of financial crises. But these countries need a well-sequenced reform agenda to attract private investment and create the growth engine that will translate hard-won gains into higher living standards.

proj-syn.title: The World Cup vs. the Extremists
proj-syn.description: Germany’s 2026 World Cup team, like so many others in the tournament, shows that loving one’s country and welcoming newcomers are not incompatible impulses. Although activists on the far left and the far right would have us believe otherwise, most ordinary people implicitly recognize this.

proj-syn.title: Beyond Brexit—and Back to Europe
proj-syn.description: Those who follow only intergovernmental negotiations or debates in the media might think that nothing has changed in the decade since the United Kingdom's voters decided to leave the European Union. Yet new polling finds that large majorities on both sides of the English Channel now support re-engagement.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s March of Folly in Iran
proj-syn.description: In promoting his “deal” with Iran, US President Donald Trump has tried to dress up a humiliating defeat as a victory. While it’s tempting to blame this outcome on incompetent leadership, it stems more from the policies and institutions that have allowed entertainers and profiteers to rise to power.
